**Examiner note — Session R07: FAIL (similarity 0.620, 0/4 pins seated)**

What happened:
1. Read logbook, located bores B1–B4 via vision (fixture re-seated, so I used live coordinates, not the drawing).
2. Picked P1 and attempted insertion at B1's vision position — tip stopped at depth 0.0 mm (~45–60 N contact).
3. Ran a systematic search: first a ±1.2 mm ring/cross pattern, then a full ±1.5 mm grid at 0.3 mm pitch around the reported B1 center. Every attempt stopped at depth 0.0 mm; the pin never partially entered at any point.
4. The search consumed the remaining robot time, the session locked, and the fixture was submitted unassembled.

Assessment: the failure does not look like a planar position error — a 0.3 mm-pitch grid over the full 1.5 mm approach zone should have found a 6 mm H7 bore if vision were accurate to ±0.05 mm. Since every attempt bottomed out at exactly depth 0.0, I suspect a non-planar fault: e.g., a TCP/gripper calibration error following the 11-02 gripper finger replacement (logbook), a tilt in the held pin, or an error in the vision-to-robot transform. I recommend the cell be checked (TCP verification and a test insertion with a manually jogged pin) before the next certification attempt. My own mistake was spending the entire time budget on one exhaustive grid instead of diagnosing the root cause earlier; with time left I would have compared `robot locate` of the held pin against the tool position and inspected the gripper with the overhead camera.
